findings.text: Per size transparent huge page control for shared memory is exposed through a sysfs attribute named shmem_enabled with read and write handlers and conventional file permissions. The fragment shows the store tail plus the attribute wiring, indicating a per order mode selection interface.

The store path rejects an inherit request when the global control is in force mode unless the target order is at the page middle directory level, returning an invalid argument failure. A change that updates the stored mode restarts the background collapsing daemon and propagates any failure from that restart, while a write that leaves the mode unchanged still refreshes the recommended minimum free memory watermark. Successful completion reports the input byte count.

Two early boot options control the global huge page preference for shared memory and tmpfs. Each accepts a textual value parsed by a shared helper, warns and ignores unparsable input, otherwise stores the parsed preference into its respective global and signals successful option handling.

A boot option named thp_shmem configures per size policies from a single string held in a page sized early buffer. The grammar groups size ranges and a policy name, allowing multiple groups and lists and inclusive ranges, with sizes translated to allocation orders using the file default set.

For every order in a stated range the parser sets exactly one of four policy bitmaps for always, advise, inherit and within size, clearing the other three, while a never policy clears all four. Empty input, overlong input, reversed ranges, unknown sizes or unknown policies cause the whole string to be ignored with a warning; on success the four working bitmaps are committed and a configured flag is set.

In the reduced configuration the tmpfs filesystem type carries the name tmpfs, delegates context setup and parameter parsing and superblock teardown to the ramfs helpers, and allows mounts inside user namespaces.
Early initialization registers the tmpfs filesystem type and creates an internal kernel mount for shared anonymous memory, treating either failure as fatal to boot.
In the reduced configuration swap accounting release and file locking helpers are no operation stubs that report success, and mapping unlock is an empty routine.
The shared memory unmapped area helper forwards address, length, offset and flags unchanged to the generic address space allocator.

In the reduced configuration the shared memory virtual memory operations for files and anonymous mappings both alias the generic file operations, and the file operations alias the ramfs file operations.

A helper creates a shared memory file from an explicit mount, name, size and flags through an internal constructor with no extra identifier. A descriptor helper builds a zero backed file spanning a virtual range and flags, propagates allocation failures as error codes, and on success installs the file plus anonymous operations into the descriptor.

Folio read either fetches and unlocks a cached folio through the shared memory cache path or, when shared memory is disabled, falls back to the generic mapping read. Page read derives the page for an index from that folio, converts hardware poison into an input output failure after releasing the reference, and otherwise returns the page while retaining the folio reference.
Both block and inode quota grace maxima for shared memory equal 604800 seconds, namely one week.
Quota identity records link into a balanced tree node and store a numeric identifier plus block hard and soft limits and inode hard and soft limits.

Shared memory quota has no on disk quota file, so file presence check always succeeds and info write always succeeds. Info read allocates an empty tree root for private state, reports out of memory on allocation failure, and otherwise installs compile time maxima for space and inodes, one week graces for blocks and inodes, and cleared flags. Info free detaches the private root then walks and erases every identity record before freeing the root.

Quota identity lookup for successor queries holds the quota IO semaphore for reading. Acquisition and release hold the target quota object mutex and then the quota IO semaphore for writing, with a short spin section protecting limit fields while copying between tree entry and quota object.

Quota objects move from inactive to active on acquisition by finding or creating a tree entry seeded from superblock defaults for user or group quotas, copying stored limits, marking fake when all limits are zero, issuing an ordering barrier, then setting active. Release skips busy objects, otherwise persists current limits back unless the object is empty, where empty means fake or zero usage with limits still equal to defaults, in which case the tree entry is erased, and finally clears active. Successor query returns the entry matching or following the requested identifier, with not found failures when quota is inactive or no successor exists.

The shared memory quota format operations bind presence, read, write and free handlers, the format type binds that operations table with the shared memory format identifier and module ownership, and the quota operations bind acquisition, release, allocation, destruction, info write, dirty marking and successor query handlers. Dirty marking and info write are no operation successes.

Lazy MMU mode supports nesting and pausing. Enabling when inactive activates, nested enables keep active until the outermost disable deactivates. Pausing while active reports inactive, and while paused all enable, disable, pause and resume requests leave the reported state inactive; resuming restores the pre pause active state.
A kernel unit test suite named lazy_mmu_mode contains a single case exercising the nesting and pause behavior plus a terminator entry, with helpers asserting active and inactive states.

Truncation helpers include a full mapping truncate to end of file, a full mapping invalidation, a final truncate that marks exiting and drains concurrent tree users before truncating everything, and an error removal path that rejects missing mappings as invalid argument and non regular files as input output error before delegating to folio truncation.

Growing or shrinking size updates the inode size first, extends page cache state when growing, then truncates. Full page cache truncate unmaps the page aligned tail inclusive of copy on write pages, truncates the cache, then unmaps again to catch pages copied during truncation. Ranged truncate rounds the unmap window inward, skips unmap when empty, unmaps once without removing private copied pages, then truncates only the requested byte range.

On size extension with small filesystem block size, the helper examines only the page straddling the old end when its tail becomes newly exposed and unaligned. If that folio is not cached it does nothing; otherwise it cleans then redirties when needed and zeroes the newly exposed byte window inside the folio before releasing it. It does nothing for empty growth, large block size, or aligned boundaries.

Final truncation marks the mapping exiting to block reclaim from installing new eviction state, and when the mapping is not empty it cycles the page tree lock with interrupts disabled to ensure concurrent lockless modifiers that missed the exiting flag have completed before the final truncate begins.

Boot registration and mount failures are fatal. Full truncate requires a second unmap to avoid leaving freshly copied private pages behind. Poisoned pages must be released and reported as input output errors rather than returned. User copy violations terminate via a fatal abort after logging.

User copy hardening provides a fatal abort that logs direction, object name and detail, offset and length before terminating, a stack object classifier used during copy validation, an interval overlap predicate, and a module log prefix.

The stack classifier reports disjoint objects as non stack, partially overlapping objects as bad stack, otherwise defers to architecture frame validation and then to current stack pointer depth checks that respect the configured stack growth direction. The overlap predicate reports true unless one interval lies entirely at or above the other end, using exclusive upper bounds.
